note: The Scattered Leaves: every piece hand-written; only the arrangement is left to seeded chance. Add pieces by hand. Never generate pieces.
slips: Ask again when the moon is thinner.
The answer is in the third drawer. It is also not.
What you are looking for is looking for you, badly, in the wrong room.
Count to nine. Then count what changed.
The box knows. The box is not saying.
Not yet. That is a complete answer.
whispers: the candle was a rumour the dark told itself
somewhere a kettle is remembering being a bell
nine swallows signed the sky and left no copy
the map apologised to the road, politely
what the well keeps is not water
a door in a field, keeping the field honest
the moon practices on the harbour first
salt, then silver, then the small hours
every staircase believes in a top floor
the orchard dreams in alphabetical order
someone left the light on in the tide
a sparrow, editing the morning
the letter arrived before it was written; we posted it anyway
gravity is just the earth, holding on
the garden keeps one bed unplanted, for guests
an echo is a voice coming back to apologise
the compass loves the north the way sailors love weather
winter keeps the receipts of every fire
a staircase of fish, ascending politely
the bell in the drowned church still keeps the hours
your name, said by rain, in another alphabet
the cat knows a fourth door and will not say
bread rising is the house, breathing in
the stars are the sky's handwriting practice
somewhere, a lighthouse is blinking in cursive
the seed does not argue with the dark; it waits in it
nine is the number the ring counts when it thinks no one is listening
the tide left a note: back soon, back always
